solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thinly populated section at the outset: do detailed analysis

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its opening, so only the leading letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of section
to parse a sentence is to analyse it grammatically in detail

explanation.surface: A survey of a sparsely inhabited district begins with close study.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparse describes something scattered thinly, as a population spread over a wide area.

clue.text: Person of note's quantity of money, we hear — big offer delights you at first

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so a word that sounds the same is wanted
at first points at the opening of each word, so the leading letters are taken

blocks.note: a sum is an amount of money
first letters of big, offer, delights and you

explanation.surface: A celebrity's fee is rumoured to be a generous offer that will delight you.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a somebody means being important or well known, a person of some standing.

clue.text: Improve image of broadcast before British race

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
B is an abbreviation for British
to rush is to race

explanation.surface: A TV channel polishes its image ahead of a British sporting race.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush a photograph is to retouch it so that it looks better.

clue.text: Discarded small piece? Not right

indicators.note: not right means the abbreviation for right is taken away

blocks.note: a shred is a tiny scrap
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A small part was thrown away because it was wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed is a past participle meaning cast off, as a snake discards its skin.

clue.text: Significant, the man's to appear ultimately in charge

indicators.note: ultimately points at the final position, so only the last letter of the word before is used

blocks.note: possessive of he
taken as written
last letter of appear
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A man is set to emerge in the end as the leader, a momentous event.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic event is one important enough to be remembered in history.

clue.text: Mysterious place, blini prepared formerly inside

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked over, so the letters are reworked into a new order
inside means placed within, so the word for formerly goes into the mix

blocks.note: taken as written
ex means former or formerly

explanation.surface: A strange restaurant where Russian pancakes used to be made on the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexplicable means impossible to explain, which makes something mysterious.

clue.text: Maybe eleven in the morning, note at the beginning

indicators.note: at the beginning means this piece is placed in front of the other

blocks.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale
am is the abbreviation for the morning hours

explanation.surface: Eleven in the morning, perhaps, with a reminder note to start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven in the morning' looks like a time; eleven is a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has eleven players, so eleven is an example of a team.

clue.text: Respond angrily referring to flipping left-winger!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: re means concerning or referring to
Trot is short for Trotskyist, a left-winger

explanation.surface: Someone snaps back at a lefty who keeps changing position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reads as a mild British expletive, as in 'that flipping lefty'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retort is to make a sharp, angry reply.

clue.text: Restriction on movement of dog? Not many in support

indicators.note: in a down answer, a support sits underneath, so this piece goes after the other

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
few means not many

explanation.surface: Should dogs be confined at night? Few people back the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an order keeping people indoors during set hours, so it limits their movement.

clue.text: Try to sell old German currency (and French)?

blocks.note: the Deutschmark, replaced by the euro
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a trader would hawk obsolete marks and francs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and French' looks like a second currency, francs; it means the French word for 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: To market a product is to promote it in order to sell it.

clue.text: Where drink may be found, stop jogging?

blocks.note: first meaning: a glass vessel for serving wine or spirits
second, whimsical meaning: de- undoes a word

explanation.surface: A runner hints that the pub is the place to quit jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke reading: a canter is a horse's easy pace, and the prefix de- reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decanter is the stoppered glass bottle that wine or port is poured into before serving.

clue.text: Warning hindmost name change is needed

indicators.note: a change alters the order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning that the last name on a list must be altered.
explanation.definitionFit: An admonishment is a reprimand or caution, a warning against bad conduct.

clue.text: Put up with tedious person

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of bear, to tolerate
second meaning: someone dull and tiresome

explanation.surface: Someone tolerated a tiresome companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Bore is the past tense of bear, to endure, and also a noun for a dull person.

clue.text: Fitting to include editor on return as expert

indicators.note: something on its return comes back the opposite way, so the editor abbreviation runs backwards
to include means to take something inside, so one word goes within another

blocks.note: apt means suitable or fitting
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: It seems right that a returning editor should be taken on as a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly skilled, which is what an expert is.

clue.text: End of street, one in France? Correct

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: last letter of street
one refers back to street; the French for street is rue

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a French address at the end of a road is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' looks like UN, French for one; here it stands for 'a street'.
explanation.definitionFit: True and correct are synonyms meaning accurate, in accordance with fact.

clue.text: Pay special attention to where tennis is played

blocks.note: first meaning: to woo or seek the favour of
second meaning: the marked playing area for tennis

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests watching the ball; the first half means wooing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to woo them with attention, and a court is also a tennis playing surface.

clue.text: Back part of boat having austere appearance

blocks.note: first meaning: the rear of a vessel
second meaning: severe and strict in manner or look

explanation.surface: The rear of a vessel looks plain and severe.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear of a ship, and stern also describes a grim, unsmiling severity.

clue.text: Record keepers, amazingly stoic with logs I'd studied from the start

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that one is taken
something amazing defies expectation, so the letters end up in a surprising new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
first letter of studied

explanation.surface: Archivists calmly sit with logbooks they have pored over from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record keepers' suggests archivists; the records are gramophone ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Discologists study and collect gramophone records, so they keep records in the musical sense.

clue.text: Cheers the Italian firm at part of arrangement put on formally?

definitions.text: part of arrangement put on formally?

blocks.note: ta is British slang for thanks
il is Italian for the
CO is the abbreviation for company
taken as written

explanation.surface: Toasting an Italian company at a formal arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' here means thanks, not a toast. The definition is cryptic: an outfit put on for formal events is an arrangement of clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailcoat is part of formal evening dress, worn with white tie on very formal occasions.

clue.text: Maltese maybe I calumniate

blocks.note: taken as written
to calumniate is to slander

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to defaming a person from Malta, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation, so a Maltese person is an example of an islander.

clue.text: They go round where many people live

definitions.text: They go round where many people live

blocks.clueFragment: They go round where many people live
blocks.note: surface reading: people doing the rounds of a crowded neighbourhood, like visitors or postmen

blocks.clueFragment: They go round where many people live
blocks.note: setter's reading: routes that encircle a city, carrying traffic around it

explanation.surface: Canvassers or delivery workers make circuits of a densely populated area.
explanation.walkthrough: London's M25 is the classic British example of a motorway encircling a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ring motorways circle large towns and cities, so they literally travel around densely inhabited places.

clue.text: Key centre of west headland

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle pair, which alone is kept

blocks.note: middle two letters of west
a cape is a headland

explanation.surface: A vital promontory in the middle of the west coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important; it is the Esc key on a computer keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Escape is the name of a keyboard key, labelled Esc, so it is an example of a key.

clue.text: Inducement of vehicle? Twaddle

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a car sales incentive as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is an incentive or reward dangled to encourage action, as in carrot and stick.

clue.text: Second horse's unexpected difficulty

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: A racehorse finishing second runs into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a hidden obstacle or problem that crops up unexpectedly.

clue.text: Country by Pacific unpleasantly cold, it's said

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the sound of the words counts rather than spelling

blocks.note: chilly means unpleasantly cold

explanation.surface: A traveller remarks that a coastal nation is unpleasantly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is the long South American nation running down the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Able to go around island

indicators.note: going around means turning about to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is free to tour an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba is the Mediterranean island where Napoleon was exiled; the palindrome 'Able was I ere I saw Elba' plays on the same pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is an Italian island off the Tuscan coast, so it is an example of an island.

clue.text: Formerly in abeyance, I overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: on ice means put on hold, suspended
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits a matter that used to be shelved was ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Once as an adverb means at some time in the past, which is what formerly means.

clue.text: Defend ourselves? Not entirely grim!

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

blocks.note: found across the end of defend and the start of ourselves

explanation.surface: A rueful question about self-defence that is only half grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Dour describes a severe, gloomy, unsmiling manner, which is grim.

clue.text: Musician, a rapper originally, with Glasgow player?

indicators.note: originally refers to where a word begins, so only its first letter is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of rapper
a player for Rangers, the Glasgow football club

explanation.surface: A musician who started out rapping now plays football in Glasgow.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is one of Glasgow's two big football clubs, so a Glasgow player is a Ranger.
explanation.definitionFit: An arranger is a musician who adapts a composition for particular instruments or voices.

clue.text: Sign of approval about sticky stuff is worthless

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: a nod signals agreement
goo is sticky muck

explanation.surface: Approving of something gummy is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no good is useless, of no value at all.

clue.text: In from France with agreement plea

blocks.note: en is French for in
a treaty is a formal agreement between states

explanation.surface: A diplomatic appeal arrives from France along with a pact.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request, which is what a plea is.

clue.text: Reportedly more important kitchen utensil

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the sound of the words is what counts

blocks.note: greater means more important

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that a certain kitchen tool matters more than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A grater is a kitchen tool with sharp holes for shredding cheese or vegetables.
